$comment: Maps each handover/<artifact>.md to the source file(s) whose contents get embedded into its
'## Code to paste into ODC' section by `npm run embed:handover` (idempotent — re-run after
editing a source file).
The project rule this serves: a handover ticket must CONTAIN the JS/CSS the developer pastes
into ODC — not just point at a repo path. A dev working inside ODC Studio cannot follow a link
into a repo they don't have open.
Entry shape — either a plain file list:
"acme-button.md": [["src/blocks/acme-button.css", "css", "Theme CSS — paste below OutSystems UI"]]
…or an object that also pins a fully-filled Mentor Studio prompt:
"acme-toast.md": {
"files": [["src/components/acme-toast.js", "js", "Script resource"]],
"mentor": { "kind": "web-component", "helper": "window.AcmeToast", "block": "Toast" }
`mentor.kind` is one of: web-component | block | restyle. When `mentor` is omitted the prompt
is derived from the artifact kind automatically.
Tokens are NOT listed here — they travel once via dist/theme.css, which is its own paste.
MARKUP IS NOT LISTED HERE EITHER. Only CSS and JS are paste targets. UI is built from native
OutSystems widgets — Containers carrying Style Classes — never from an HTML string dropped
into an Expression. Embedding a .html file here invites exactly that: it presents markup as
something to paste. See the warning section in handover/odc-palette-screen.md for what that
cost on sg-palette-specimen (a screen shipped rendering its own tags as visible text, with a
clean build gate and a Mentor turn reporting success).
Add an entry for every new handover. A handover with no entry gets no embedded code, and the
embed silently goes stale when its source changes — so keep this in sync (the build warns).
